Oil was found at Dukhan, on the west coast of Qatar, in 1939. The Second World War held up production, and the first exports left in 1949.

Qatar had been one of the poorest places in the Gulf. The pearl trade had collapsed in the 1930s, and many families had left. Oil money changed that within a generation: the ruling Al Thani family built schools, hospitals and a new Doha.

Dukhan is still Qatar's main onshore oil field. But the country's great fortune came later, from gas in the North Field, found in 1971, which made Qatar one of the richest countries in the world per head. The oil company was taken over by the state in the 1970s.
